coverage: Reconciled both completed blind reports (GPT-6 Sol: 1 finding; Claude Opus 5.5: 3 findings) against all 9 criteria with polarity and points, the native shared role prompt, the closed-universe assignment-4 prompt with stipulations, and the three prior prompts. Read the Bell supplemental disclosure ¶¶ 1-4 in full, the Britt comparator memorandum header and ¶¶ 1-6, PERB ¶ 2, and the earlier Award and Final Notice passages from the extractions. Public-policy rulings rely on the W.R. Grace and Misco framework quoted in the blind reports and on the criteria themselves; this pass did not reread those uploaded opinions. The pinned native judge templates show that penalty criteria pass only when the response commits the stated failure, and that the judge sees only the criterion text. No solver or judge was run.

verdicts.reason: Agree. Bell ¶ 1 refers to an 'April 17, 2024 comparator memorandum,' but the Britt memorandum is dated April 11, 2024, so the discrepancy is real. The prompt asks how Kucera changes the scope, burden, preservation, and exception analysis, and the misdating affects none of those questions. The prompt's instruction to 'Support every point with page and paragraph citations' and the exact document name, which includes 'Apr. 11, 2024,' make noticing the error ordinary cite-checking diligence. Reasonable litigators could differ on whether omitting it is a deficiency. Consolidated with Opus O1.
Same ground as Sol F1, consolidated in R1. Weight is the main aggravating factor: criterion 8 is worth 28 of 73 positive points, more than any substantive criterion in the assignment.

Agree at arguable. 'Holds each of MPD's arguments' has no settled meaning. It could mean that the comparator leaves every argument intact, supports every argument, or bears on every argument. The judge receives only this text, so it cannot use the justification to resolve the ambiguity. The misfire risk is limited: a competent response says the factor-six position is weakened, so it is unlikely to be read as saying every argument 'holds' in either sense. That limited risk is why this is arguable rather than problematic.

Overturned. Under the W.R. Grace and Misco test reflected in the uploads, a public policy must be well defined and dominant and must be ascertained from laws and legal precedents. The test asks whether enforcing the award violates that policy. It does not ask how MPD has disciplined other officers. Kucera is also outside the arbitration record, as Bell ¶ 4 says. Criterion 9 therefore takes the legally correct, or at least reasonable, side. A careful response can also mention the practical credibility risk Opus identifies and still say that the doctrinal public-policy argument does not depend on comparator evidence; such a response would satisfy the criterion. Under the Harvey definition, a criterion that takes a reasonable side of a judgment call is not defective. 'Unsupported_fact' is also the wrong category, because the criterion does not assert a fact.

findings.title: Criterion 8 assigns 28 points to an immaterial misdating of the Britt memorandum in the Bell disclosure
findings.explanation: This consolidates Sol F1 and Opus O1. Criterion 8 requires a response to identify that the Supplemental Disclosure 'misdates the comparator memorandum it references.' Bell ¶ 1 refers to the 'April 17, 2024 comparator memorandum,' while the Britt memorandum is dated April 11, 2024. The prompt asks how Kucera changes the scope-of-review, burden, preservation, contrary-to-law, and public-policy analysis, and whether Kucera can be considered on review. The date error changes none of those answers. The justification relies only on the general direction to 'Support every point with page and paragraph citations.' An associate who cites the Britt memorandum by its exact listed name, which includes 'Apr. 11, 2024,' may notice the error, and noting it is good practice. Omitting it, however, does not make any requested answer wrong. Because the item outweighs every substantive criterion in the assignment, reasonable graders could differ on whether it measures diligence or an unrequested requirement. The issue is therefore arguable.

findings.title: The -16 penalty's 'holds each of MPD's arguments' is too indeterminate to apply predictably
findings.explanation: This is Opus O2; Sol did not flag the issue. Criterion 5 deducts 16 points if a response 'Mentions that the supplemental comparator document holds each of MPD's arguments.' 'Holds' could mean that Kucera leaves every argument intact, that Kucera supports every argument, or that Kucera bears on every argument. The justification links the penalty to the prompt's question about which arguments survive and which are weakened, which suggests the intended failure is saying that nothing is weakened. The native penalty judge sees only the criterion text and is told to 'Answer Pass only if the response DOES commit this failure.' The penalty could therefore misfire on a response that says Kucera bears on each argument in different ways, or it could miss the intended error when that error is worded differently. A competent response that says factor six is weakened is unlikely to trigger it under any reading, so the defect is arguable rather than problematic.
